key_insight: Kriging and neural-network surrogates can predict pressure losses across perforated plates more accurately than standard empirical formulas, even with limited experimental data.
engineering_relevance: The models provide a practical way to improve pressure-drop estimation and CFD source-term modeling for perforated-plate flows in turbulent industrial systems.
method: Train two data-driven models (kriging and NN) on published experimental pressure-loss datasets.
Compare predictions against common empirical correlations across multiple perforated-plate configurations.
Embed the learned pressure-loss relation as a momentum-source term in 2D RANS channel-flow simulations.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that both models were evaluated on two experimental datasets and consistently outperformed widely used empirical formulae, with good agreement to measurements and RANS results.
watch_item: Performance is encouraging but the training data are limited and drawn from sparse literature measurements, so extrapolation to unseen geometries or flow conditions may be unreliable.
paper_title: Kriging and neural network models for pressure losses across perforated plates
